question: Can learning a distributed word representation jointly with a neural next-word probability function fight the curse of dimensionality and beat smoothed n-gram language models?
hypothesis: Similar words get nearby feature vectors, and a smooth probability function over them lets each training sentence inform exponentially many neighbouring sentences, improving generalisation and use of longer contexts.
contributions: Joint learning of word feature vectors C and a neural probability function g
Large-scale training (millions of parameters) with data-parallel and parameter-parallel implementations
Perplexity gains over state-of-the-art n-grams on Brown and AP News, with benefit from longer context

method.summary: Feed-forward network: each of the n-1 context words is mapped through a shared |V| x m lookup matrix C, concatenated, passed through an optional tanh hidden layer and optional direct linear connections, then a softmax over the vocabulary. Trained by stochastic gradient ascent on penalised log-likelihood, optionally mixed with an interpolated trigram.

datasets.name: Brown corpus
datasets.size: 1,181,041 words; 47,578 distinct words reduced to |V|=16,383 (frequency <=3 merged into one symbol)
datasets.split: first 800,000 train, next 200,000 validation, last 181,041 test
datasets.preprocessing: case kept, punctuation and text/paragraph separators kept as tokens; words with frequency <=3 merged into a single symbol

datasets.name: AP News 1995-1996
datasets.size: train 13,994,528 words; validation 963,138; test 963,071; 148,721 distinct words reduced to |V|=17,964
datasets.preprocessing: kept most frequent words and punctuation, lowercased, numeric forms mapped to special symbols, rare words to a special symbol, proper nouns to another special symbol

models.name: Neural probabilistic LM (MLP1-MLP10)
models.params: inferred: formula |V|(1+nm+h)+h(1+(n-1)m); for AP net (|V|=17,964,n=6,h=60,m=100) about 11.3M by that formula, paper says largest network is almost 100 megabytes
models.architecture: shared word-feature lookup C, tanh hidden layer, optional direct connections, softmax output
models.init_from: random initialisation of word features and weights
models.layers: one tanh hidden layer plus linear shared feature layer
models.context: n=3 or 5 (Brown), n=6 (AP), i.e. n-1 previous words

other.Brown configs: MLP1-2 n5 h50 m60 direct; MLP3-4 n5 h0 m60 direct; MLP5-6 n5 h50 m30 direct; MLP7-8 n3 h50 m30 direct; MLP9-10 n5 h100 m30 no direct; even numbers are mixed with trigram

models.name: Interpolated (deleted interpolation) trigram
models.architecture: mixture of uniform, unigram, bigram, trigram with weights conditional on discretised context frequency, weights fit by EM (~5 iterations) on validation set

models.name: Class-based n-gram (SRILM)
models.architecture: class-based back-off n-gram; classes 150-2000, orders 3 to 5

training.objective: maximise penalised log-likelihood L = (1/T) sum_t log f(w_t, ...; theta) + R(theta)
training.optimizer: stochastic gradient ascent, one update per word, asynchronous or parameter-parallel
training.lr: initial 1e-3, eps_t = eps_0/(1+r t) with r=1e-8
training.lr_schedule: eps_t = eps_0 / (1 + r t), t = number of parameter updates
training.epochs: Brown: apparent convergence after about 10 to 20 epochs; AP: 5 epochs
training.weight_decay: 1e-4 (Brown), 1e-5 (AP), applied to weights and C, not biases
training.regularisation: weight decay; early stopping on validation (needed only on Brown)
training.hardware: cluster of 1.2 GHz Athlon processors (32 x 2 CPUs), Myrinet network, MPI; 40 CPUs for AP run
training.compute: AP: 5 epochs in approximately three weeks with 40 CPUs

other.mixing: NN probabilities mixed with interpolated trigram at fixed weight 0.5 (tables), or learned weight / frequency-conditional weights
other.softmax stability: subtract max of y_j before exponentiating (extra Allreduce)

metrics.name: test perplexity
metrics.definition: geometric average of 1/P(w_t|w_1^{t-1}), exponential of average negative log-likelihood; all tokens including punctuation treated alike, no special end-of-sentence handling

eval.protocol: single runs reported; validation set used for model selection, weight decay, early stopping, n-gram order and class count; no seeds or significance tests stated

evidence.quote: the initial learning rate was set to εo = 10−3
The last three columns give perplexity on the training, validation and test sets.
evidence.where: Table 1 caption; Table 2 rows have only two numbers (valid, test inferred)

results.claim: On Brown, the best neural net (MLP10, mixed 0.5 with interpolated trigram) reaches test perplexity 252 versus 312 for the best n-gram (class-based back-off, 500 classes), about 24% lower.
results.setup: Brown corpus, 800,000 train / 200,000 validation / 181,041 test words, |V|=16,383; test perplexity (lower is better); MLP10: n=5, h=100, m=30, no direct connections, mix yes
results.note: Column assignment (valid vs test) inferred from the flattened table and the caption's 33%/24% figures: 336/252=1.33, 312/252=1.24.

results.claim: Neural net beats best n-gram by about 24% test perplexity on Brown and about 8% on AP News.
results.metric: relative test perplexity gap vs best-on-validation n-gram
results.setup: Brown corpus, 800,000 train / 200,000 validation / 181,041 test words, |V|=16,383; test perplexity (lower is better) and AP News 1995-96, 13,994,528 train words, |V|=17,964; test perplexity, 5 epochs, ~3 weeks on 40 CPUs
results.quote: with a test perplexity difference of about 24% on

results.claim: On AP News, MLP10 (n=6, h=60, m=100, direct, mixed) gets test perplexity 109 vs 117 for the 5-gram modified Kneser-Ney back-off and 132 for the deleted-interpolation trigram.
results.setup: AP News 1995-96, 13,994,528 train words, |V|=17,964; test perplexity, 5 epochs, ~3 weeks on 40 CPUs
results.note: Text says 8% gap; 117/109 is about 7%, 119/109 about 9%; the paper's 8% is not exactly reproduced from the table as flattened. Column order valid/test inferred.

results.claim: The neural net gain over the interpolated trigram on Brown: trigram test perplexity is 33% above the lowest-validation neural net.
results.setup: Brown corpus, 800,000 train / 200,000 validation / 181,041 test words, |V|=16,383; test perplexity (lower is better)
results.quote: plexity that is 33% above that of the neural network with the lowest validation perplexity.

results.setup: Brown corpus, 800,000 train / 200,000 validation / 181,041 test words, |V|=16,383; test perplexity (lower is better)

results.claim: Parameter count formula is |V|(1+nm+h)+h(1+(n-1)m), dominated by |V|(nm+h); scales linearly in |V| and n.
Output-layer weighted sums are about 99.7% of per-example computation for the AP network (|V|=17,964, h=60, n=6, m=100).
Parameter-parallel training on 1.2 GHz Athlon cluster (32 x 2 CPUs, Myrinet) had communication overhead of only 1/15 of epoch time, near-perfect speed-up.
results.setup: AP News 1995-96, 13,994,528 train words, |V|=17,964; test perplexity, 5 epochs, ~3 weeks on 40 CPUs
results.quote: communication overhead was only 1/15th of the total time

results.claim: Unsurprising negative result: fixed word features from principal components of co-occurrence counts (LSI-like) did not work; joint learning of features and model was useful.
results.quote: We tried (unsuccessfully) using as ﬁxed word features

results.claim: Conclusion: improvement over smoothed trigram is between 10 and 20% in perplexity.
Curse-of-dimensionality example: joint over 10 words with |V|=100,000 has about 10^50 - 1 free parameters.
results.note: Printed as 10000010-1 = 1050-1 due to lost superscripts.

results.claim: Importance-sampling training speed-up of 100-fold is cited (Bengio and Senecal 2003).
results.setup: energy-based variant, cited not run here

limits: Training cost: AP run took three weeks on 40 CPUs for 5 epochs; authors say the model is expensive and needs speed-ups
Only fixed small windows (n up to 6); no long-context mechanism, recurrence suggested as future work
Polysemous words get a single vector (authors concede)
Word vectors randomly initialised; knowledge-based init untested
Single runs, no variance reported; Table 2 gain is 8%, smaller on the larger corpus
Quantitative evaluation is perplexity only; no downstream task (speech recognition cited to Schwenk and Gauvain 2002)
Learned word vectors are not inspected or evaluated
